*   **Performance:** Improves load balancing in parallel environments by reducing idle time caused by uneven distribution of isosurface complexity across sub-blocks [S1, S2].

Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly state that the merging strategy is designed to address the issue of uneven distribution of extraction times (complexity) among sub-blocks. They note that merging only brothers can lead to idle time waiting for the slower block. By allowing merges with nephews (or brother's children) that share a common border, the system can balance the load more effectively, thereby reducing idle time in parallel environments. The claim accurately reflects the stated purpose and mechanism in the evidence.
